samples.question: The picture is a single row of cream panels, acted on from left to right as the arrow beneath the row shows. The leftmost panel, the one drawn inside a dark ring, holds a coloured square: that is the colour the paint pot holds before anything happens. Every panel to its right is a card, and the cards act on the pot one at a time in drawn left-to-right order. A card holding a coloured circle is a paint card: it paints the pot that colour. A card holding a dark grey left-pointing triangle is an undo card: it cancels the most recent paint card that has already acted and has not itself already been cancelled, so the pot goes back to the colour it held just before that paint card acted; if every paint card that has acted has already been cancelled, the undo card changes nothing. A paint card counts as still in effect once it has acted and has not been cancelled. The colour the pot holds at the end is not drawn anywhere in the picture. What colour does the paint pot hold after the last card has acted? Answer with one word: red, blue, green, amber or violet.
